title: Creation: In the Beginning
style: Cinematic 3D biblical realism. Highly detailed environments and physically believable materials. Natural skin and cloth. Dramatic volumetric light. Warm amber and burnt-orange highlights used sparingly, earthy browns and greens, gentle cool shadows, rich blacks, restrained cinematic grade. Do not apply a heavy orange filter. Vertical 9:16 composition. Feature-film quality.
narration: Before Adam. Before Noah. Before Abraham. Before there was a single person on earth, there was God. And the Bible opens with these words: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.

scenes.narration: Before Adam. Before Noah. Before Abraham. Before there was a single person on earth, there was God. And the Bible opens with these words: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
scenes.visual: A vast primordial earth before human civilization, formless and empty, darkness covering an immense deep ocean, no buildings, no people, no modern objects, mysterious biblical creation atmosphere, enormous scale, cinematic wide shot, subtle warm amber highlights emerging at the edges of darkness.

scenes.narration: The earth was formless and empty. Darkness covered the deep. And the Spirit of God was over the waters.
scenes.visual: Endless primordial waters stretching beneath deep darkness, powerful gentle movement across the surface, the Spirit of God represented only by a subtle majestic presence moving over the waters, no human form invented, awe-inspiring scale, volumetric atmosphere, restrained amber light.

scenes.narration: Then God spoke. Let there be light. And there was light. God separated the light from the darkness.
scenes.visual: Brilliant divine light suddenly breaking through absolute primordial darkness above the waters, breathtaking transformation from darkness into radiant light, strong volumetric rays, vast cinematic composition, warm golden amber highlights without an orange color cast.

scenes.narration: Then God made the sky. He gathered the waters together, and dry land appeared.
scenes.visual: Primordial waters separating as dry land rises across a vast new world, distant sky opening above, rivers and coastlines forming naturally, immense landscape, cinematic aerial perspective, realistic water and stone, warm sunlight beginning to illuminate the land.

scenes.narration: Then the earth brought forth vegetation: plants, trees, and seed-bearing life covering the land.
scenes.visual: A newly formed landscape coming alive with dense green vegetation, young trees and plants spreading naturally across fertile land, morning sunlight passing through leaves, detailed soil and foliage, cinematic depth, subtle warm amber sunlight.

scenes.narration: Then came the lights of the heavens: the sun, the moon, and the stars, marking the day and the night.
scenes.visual: Majestic cinematic view of the ordered heavens, brilliant sun above the horizon, moon visible across the sky, countless stars appearing in the deep heavens, realistic celestial scale, atmospheric depth, warm solar glow with restrained orange highlights.

scenes.narration: The waters filled with living creatures. Birds filled the sky. Then land animals appeared across the earth, each according to its kind.
scenes.visual: Breathtaking living world filled with sea creatures beneath clear waters, birds sweeping through a vast sky, diverse land animals moving across open grasslands, lush vegetation and mountains in the distance, realistic anatomy and natural behavior, cinematic wildlife photography feel.

scenes.narration: Then God created humanity in His image, male and female. And when God saw everything He had made, He saw that it was very good.
scenes.visual: A newly created man and woman standing together in an untouched natural world, shown respectfully and without invented clothing or physical details beyond what Scripture establishes, vast beautiful creation surrounding them, peaceful sunrise, warm amber rim light, cinematic wide shot, sense of awe and completion.

cta: Follow Kindled Iron. Next, we meet Adam.
